meta.title: Early Collision-Risk Prediction from Real ESA Conjunction Data Linked to Simulated RGB-YOLO Perception and Minimum-Δv Avoidance Maneuver Selection
meta.description: Student research prototype: real ESA conjunction data for early collision-risk prediction, linked to simulated onboard RGB-YOLO perception, tracking and minimum-Δv avoidance maneuver selection.

home.title: Early Collision-Risk Prediction from Real ESA Conjunction Data Linked to Simulated RGB-YOLO Perception and Minimum-Δv Avoidance Maneuver Selection
home.lead: Satellite operators must decide whether to maneuver about two days before the closest approach to a piece of space debris, while the collision risk is still uncertain. This project assesses that risk early from real ESA conjunction messages. When the risk is high, it triggers a simulated onboard camera chain (YOLO detection, tracking, bearing estimation) and searches for the smallest velocity change (Δv) that makes the encounter safe. Results are shown both with perfect information and with realistic perception errors.
home.real: ESA Collision Avoidance Challenge conjunction data (CDMs) and the collision-risk prediction experiment, including the official-test evaluation. The maneuver experiments use the real encounter geometry of these events.
home.sim: RGB imagery, the YOLO onboard-vision experiment, the tracking sequences, and maneuver execution. ESA provides no images, and no real spacecraft was maneuvered.
home.k1: official ESA score of the latest-risk baseline
home.s1: REAL · lower is better; no ML model beat it
home.k4: maneuver plans still safe with realistic perception error
home.s4: SIMULATED · 10 km tracking, 3σ margin (100% with perfect information)

problem.title: Problem
problem.p1: Thousands of tracked debris objects cross the orbits of active satellites. For each close approach (a conjunction), operators receive a sequence of Conjunction Data Messages (CDMs). Each CDM predicts the miss distance, the uncertainty of both positions and a collision probability.
problem.p2: The risk is only well known shortly before the time of closest approach (TCA). A maneuver, however, has to be planned and approved earlier, typically about two days before TCA. Early CDMs are uncertain: the reported risk can rise or fall sharply in the last day.
problem.p3: Prediction alone is therefore not sufficient. A warning has to lead to an action (more observation, onboard sensing, maneuver planning), and that action must remain safe when its inputs contain errors. This project studies the full chain and measures where it is strong and where it is weak.
problem.fig: REAL ESA event: CDM-reported risk over time. Only CDMs at least 2 days before TCA are used as input; the final value (star) is the label to be predicted.

data.title: ESA data
data.banner: REAL DATA — ESA Collision Avoidance Challenge (Kelvins), CDMs from 2015–2019
data.p1: The official dataset is published by ESA on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.4463683, CC BY 4.0). It is not re-hosted here. Each row is one CDM with 103 recorded quantities; {{esa_data.train_file_cdms}} CDMs in {{esa_data.train_file_events}} events form the training file.
terms: CDM (Conjunction Data Message): one forecast of a close approach, with miss distance, relative speed, position uncertainties and collision probability.
Event: all CDMs about the same close approach, ordered in time.
Target: the ESA satellite being protected. Chaser: the other object (debris, rocket body, payload or unknown).
TCA: time of closest approach; each CDM states how many days remain until TCA.
Final risk: the log10 collision probability in the last CDM of an event (less than 1 day before TCA). An event is high-risk if the final risk ≥ 10⁻⁶ (the challenge definition).
protocol: Inputs: only CDMs released at least 2 days before TCA; the final CDM is never an input.
Training events: {{esa_data.train_eligible_events}} eligible events, of which only {{esa_data.train_eligible_high_risk}} are high-risk.
Official held-out test set: {{esa_data.test_events}} events ({{esa_data.test_high_risk}} high-risk) with labels released by ESA after the competition. It was used once, for final evaluation only.
Splitting is by event, never by row, and model thresholds come from cross-validation on training events only.
data.fig: REAL ESA data: distribution of the final risk (log scale). The dashed line marks the high-risk boundary 10⁻⁶.

pred.title: AI risk prediction
pred.banner: REAL DATA — evaluated on the official ESA test set ({{esa_data.test_events}} events, {{esa_data.test_high_risk}} high-risk)
pred.p1: Four approaches were compared using 26 interpretable features from the CDMs available two days before TCA: (A) the latest reported risk, the published baseline; (B) logistic regression with 3 features; (C) Random Forest; (D) XGBoost. F2 weights recall more than precision, because missing a dangerous event is worse than a false alarm. PR-AUC measures how well events are ranked. The official ESA competition score is MSE_HR / F2 (lower is better).
pred.neg: The machine-learning classifiers tested in this project did not outperform the published latest-risk baseline on the official ESA competition score ({{official_metric.A_latest_risk_baseline.score_MSE_HR_over_F2|3}} for the baseline vs {{official_metric.C_random_forest.score_MSE_HR_over_F2|3}} for the best classifier). The baseline result reproduces the published value exactly.
pred.roles: Random Forest provided stronger event ranking by PR-AUC ({{prediction.official_test.C_random_forest.pr_auc|3}} vs {{prediction.official_test.A_latest_risk_baseline.pr_auc|3}}). It can be interpreted as a prioritisation signal (which events to observe first), not as proof that it replaces the baseline trigger. The latest-risk rule remains the strongest trigger.
pred.fig_pr: Precision–recall curves on the official test set.
pred.fig_early: Earlier warnings are harder: F2 when deciding 2–5 days before TCA.
pred.decision_p: Predictions are mapped to CONTINUE MONITORING, PREPARE / OBSERVE, or HIGH-RISK TRIGGER. The evaluated layer uses the Random Forest rule that was fixed by training cross-validation before the test set was opened. It triggered {{decision.trigger_tp_fp_fn.0}} of {{esa_data.test_high_risk}} high-risk events with {{decision.trigger_tp_fp_fn.1}} false alarms. All thresholds are experimental design values, not operational rules.

vision.title: RGB-YOLO perception
vision.banner: SIMULATED RGB EXPERIMENT — synthetic images with exact ground truth
vision.p1: A pinhole-camera renderer creates synthetic onboard scenes of satellites, debris fragments and rocket bodies. It varies apparent size (3–220 px), attitude, sunlight, exposure, star fields, Earth limb, blur and sensor noise, and records the exact position of the object. The images were split into {{yolo.dataset.train.images}} training, {{yolo.dataset.val.images}} validation and {{yolo.dataset.test.images}} held-out test scenes, plus a controlled difficulty sweep.
vision.p2: A COCO-pretrained YOLO26-nano detector was fine-tuned on these images (not trained from scratch). On held-out synthetic test images it reached mAP50 = {{yolo.test.mAP50|3}}. Very small, dim or noisy targets are often missed, and some star-like false detections occur; genuine failure examples are shown below.
vision.fig_examples: SIMULATED examples (green = ground truth, red = YOLO). Top row: easy, medium and two hard cases. Bottom row: two missed objects and two false detections. Failures are shown on purpose.
vision.fig_sweep: SIMULATED controlled sweep: detection recall vs target size, exposure and sensor noise (40 images per point, 95% intervals).

tracking.title: Multi-frame tracking and bearing
tracking.p1: YOLO runs on every frame. A Kalman filter links consecutive detections into a track, and the camera geometry converts each tracked pixel into a bearing (line-of-sight direction). Estimates are compared with the simulator's ground truth.
tracking.range_title: A single monocular RGB camera measures direction (bearing), not direct physical range.
tracking.range: An exploratory experiment estimated range from apparent size with an assumed object size. It had a median error of about {{tracking.exploratory_range_from_apparent_size.range_rel_error_median|pct0}} even when the object size was known exactly, so it is not the basis of any safety claim.
tracking.fig: SIMULATED sequence: bearing angles (azimuth and elevation) of the ground truth and of the Kalman track over time, with the per-frame bearing error.

maneuver.title: Maneuver selection
maneuver.banner: SIMULATED MANEUVER EXPERIMENT — on the real encounter geometry of triggered ESA events
maneuver.p1: For each triggered test event, the real CDM geometry (miss vector, relative velocity, covariances, object sizes) is used to evaluate 1,830 candidate impulses: 5 execution times (2 days to 6 hours before TCA) × 6 directions (radial, along-track and cross-track, each ±) × 61 Δv magnitudes. Clohessy–Wiltshire relative-motion equations give the satellite's displacement at TCA; the new miss distance and collision probability are then recomputed.
maneuver.p2: A candidate is safe if the miss distance ≥ {{maneuver.safe_miss_m|0}} m and the collision probability ≤ 10⁻⁶ (experimental design thresholds). The safe candidate with the smallest Δv is selected.
perfect: Median selected Δv: {{maneuver.dv_median_mps|cms}} cm/s; along-track burns were always the cheapest, and earlier burns cost less.
realistic: The cheapest plan sits exactly on the safety limit, so estimation errors matter.

With the typical bearing error at a 10 km tracking range and a 3σ safety margin, {{error_propagation.safe_rate.typical_10km_k3|pct}} of plans remained safe ({{error_propagation.safe_rate.typical_10km_k0|pct}} without the margin).
Including tracking failures: {{error_propagation.safe_rate.with_failures_10km_k3|pct}} safe with the margin.
maneuver.fig_plane: SIMULATED maneuver on REAL geometry (ESA event 880, perfect information): encounter plane before (red) and after (green), with 1σ/3σ uncertainty ellipses and the 1 km safety circle.
maneuver.fig_lead: Minimum safe Δv vs execution time for all triggered events that needed a maneuver (perfect information).

demo.title: Interactive demo (precomputed)
demo.intro: Step through the full chain for real ESA test events. Each event shows the real CDM history and prediction. Only triggered events continue into the simulated camera and maneuver steps.
demo.precomputed: All values were computed in advance by the project's verified pipeline. The website does not train or run any model.

explain.s1: Real ESA event {event_id}: {n_cdms} CDMs released at least 2 days before closest approach. Each point is the risk reported in one CDM. The dashed red line is the high-risk boundary.
explain.s2: The Random Forest reads features from these CDMs and outputs P(high final risk) = {prob}. The trigger threshold {thr} was chosen by cross-validation on training events only. The latest reported risk is 10^{latest}.
explain.s3: Decision: {state}. Ground truth, hidden from the model: the final risk was 10^{final} ({truth}). Low-risk events stop here and are only monitored.
explain.s4: The trigger starts the SIMULATED onboard camera: {frames} synthetic frames of an approaching object. Drag the slider or press play. These images are generated by our renderer; they are not ESA imagery.
explain.s5: The fine-tuned YOLO finds the object in {det}% of frames (green = detected, red = missed). Early frames are missed because the object is only a few pixels wide.
explain.s6: The Kalman filter turns noisy detections into a smooth track (orange) that follows the true image path (grey). Median detection-centre error: {center} px.
explain.s7: Camera intrinsics convert each tracked pixel into line-of-sight angles. Bearing error RMSE {brmse}°. Exploratory only: range from apparent size with an assumed size gives a predicted closest approach of {pmiss} m vs {tmiss} m true; no safety decision relies on this.
explain.s8: {nc} candidate maneuvers on the REAL encounter geometry: each line is one direction, and the dashed line is the required distance ({safe} m + {margin} m perception margin).
explain.s9: Selected (red circle): {dir} burn of {dv} cm/s, {lead} days before TCA. It is the smallest Δv that satisfies both the distance and the Pc constraints ({ns} of {nc} candidates are safe).
explain.s10: Encounter plane before (red, miss {miss0} m, Pc {pc0}) and after (green, miss {miss1} m, Pc {pc1}). Ellipses are 1σ and 3σ uncertainty; the dotted circle is the {safe} m safety distance; the black dot is the combined object size.

limits.title: Limitations
items: The machine-learning models did not beat the ESA latest-risk baseline on the official competition metric (or on F2); they only ranked events better.
Only {{esa_data.train_eligible_high_risk}} high-risk training events exist after the official rules, and warnings 3–5 days ahead are clearly weaker.
YOLO can miss very small, dim or noisy targets, and it produces some star-like false detections.
The tracker failed on {{tracking.sequences_with_track_failure}} of {{tracking.n_sequences}} tested sequences (it locked onto a false detection).
A monocular RGB camera does not directly provide range; the apparent-size range estimate has substantial error (about {{tracking.exploratory_range_from_apparent_size.range_rel_error_median|pct0}}).
The images are synthetic and the visual scenario is slow and close-range, whereas real conjunctions occur at about {{maneuver.median_relative_speed_kms|0}} km/s.
The maneuver model is simplified (Clohessy–Wiltshire dynamics, no drag or J2; approximate collision probability; experimental thresholds).
Nominal minimum-Δv solutions may lose safety under perception errors (see the realistic-error result).
This is a research simulation, not flight-qualified software. No real spacecraft was maneuvered.

Classifiers submit the latest reported risk when they flag an event and −6.001 otherwise (fixed before evaluation).
